purpose: Executable narrative-similarity pilot. Each version is read from an identified passage in the v2 corpus and each event carries the passage id and a verbatim quote supporting it. Annotations are analyst-written from the translated source and are review_state=source_verified (transcription bound), not independently_annotated (second coder pending).

review_state_definitions.transcribed: Annotation content taken directly from the cited passage.
review_state_definitions.source_verified: Cited passage id and quote were machine-checked against corpus offsets by tools/validate_annotations.py.
review_state_definitions.independently_annotated: A second coder produced the same coding without seeing this file. NOT YET DONE for any version in this pilot.

coding_manual.predicate_vocabulary_note: Closed vocabulary. A predicate is an action or change of state that the cited text explicitly narrates or explicitly alludes to. Interpretive summaries are not predicates.
coding_manual.alignment_note: Needleman-Wunsch over event sequences in narrated order. Mismatch cost c(a,b) = 1 - event similarity, where event similarity is the weighted mean of predicate (0.50), participant-role matching (0.30) and outcome overlap (0.20) over whichever of those parts are measurable on both sides; an unmeasurable part drops out of the average instead of contributing zero, so that missing coding is never read as narrative difference. Costs are in [0,1]; gaps cost the preregistered penalty. S_sequence = 1 - D_mn / max(m,n).

protocol_revisions.change: Comparison-class checklists added, so a motif counts as an adjudicated absence only when the coder looked for it; cross-class motif comparisons return NA.
protocol_revisions.reason: First run left 68 of 91 pairs without a motif score because per-version motif lists were sparse and non-overlapping, conflating 'not compared' with 'not present'.

protocol_revisions.change: Needleman-Wunsch traceback bug fixed: the two gap directions were swapped relative to the dynamic-program option order, so the emitted alignment was not a valid monotone path and mislabelled which events were matched. A replay assertion now recomputes the DP cost from the emitted path and rejects any mislabelling.
protocol_revisions.reason: Found by the unit test suite, not by the scores: S_sequence itself was correct because it reads the cost matrix, so the defect was invisible in every number published before it.
protocol_revisions.affects: aligned_event_pairs, alignment_gaps, aligned_event_ids. No score changes.

protocol_revisions.change: Event similarity renormalises over measurable parts rather than scoring an uncoded outcome as maximal difference.
protocol_revisions.reason: An event with no coded outcome could not exceed 0.8 against a copy of itself, so annotation completeness was leaking into the score as narrative dissimilarity.
protocol_revisions.affects: S_sequence and every event-level comparison; the 0.50/0.30/0.20 weights are unchanged and none were refitted.

coding_manual.protocol_revision_note: The scoring weights below were fixed before the first pair score was computed and have not been changed. The revisions above change what is measured, not how much each part counts, and each is recorded with its date and reason so the first run's numbers are not silently overwritten.
coding_manual.motif_weight_note: Diagnosticity weights are preregistered analyst judgements, capped at 1.0, with common motifs weighted low. They are NOT fitted to any outcome. Sensitivity analysis varies them; leave-one-region-out re-derives them empirically.
coding_manual.unknown_vs_absent_note: A motif not annotated is 'unassessed' when the cited attestation is partial; the engine emits NA rather than treating absence as evidence of difference.

alignment_weights.note: Preregistered on 1 November 2026 before any pair score was computed. None of these values were fitted to an outcome. The sensitivity sweep varies gap_penalty and predicate_credit.same_family and reports how much the ranking moves.

coding_manual.referent_note: referent is a coder assertion of narrative identity, not a string match on the translation's wording. Two participants count as the same only if the coder says so; matching on role and referent_kind alone  earns partial credit, so Thor and Indra are not equated for being storm deities.
coding_manual.comparison_class_note: Motif comparison is only defined inside a comparison class, because a motif can only be scored as absent when the coder actually looked for it. Each class carries a fixed checklist, so every version in that class adjudicates the same motifs and two versions in different classes return NA rather than a spuriously low score.
